|A Lasso Duel
|The Western Democrat and the Daily Nashville Patriot
|May 24, and June 4, 1861
|Charlotte, North Carolina, and Nashville, Tennessee
|
|Two men in Arizona, a Mexican and a boatman from Mississippi, engaged in a 'lasso duel" while on horseback. The white man won and killed the Mexican.
|
|-
|A Stone Falls from the Sky, with characters engraved upon it
|The Daily Phoenix and the St. Louis Democrat
|November 5, 1861
|Phoenix, Arizona and St. Louis, Missouri
|
|An elderly fur trapper named James Lumley was hunting in upper Missouri in September of 1861, when he spotted a "bright luminous body in the heavens" crash in the middle of the woods. When Mr. Lumley went to investigate, he found an object in the shape of an "immense stone driven into the side of a mountain." When Mr. Lumley investigated the site, he found several hieroglyphs, strange glass-like materials, and dark stains from an unknown liquid.

|We Can Have a Navy in the Air
|The Morning Times
|April 12, 1896
|Washington, D.C.

|An unnamed professor discusses and displays his idea for a flying machine capable of aerial combat,which was announced to be completed on January 1, 1900.

|He Died Anyway
|The Daily Herald
|September 11, 1896
|Brownsville, Texas
|
|On September 8, 1896, an elderly man from Burton, Texas named Schoneberg, fell unconscious and was presumed dead. However, on the day of his funeral, he arose from his coffin and left. The following day, September 9th, he once again fell unconscious and died.
